components.description: RPO: learning only the root routing token for adaptive reasoning

nodes.name: Overthinking in LRMs
nodes.description: Large reasoning models apply long explicit <think> reasoning uniformly regardless of query complexity, wasting compute and latency on trivial questions.

nodes.name: Prior policy-optimization hurdles
nodes.description: Prior approaches to learning when to reason suffer from training inefficiency (long-trajectory GRPO has prohibitive VRAM and time cost), data curation difficulty, and an initialization gap from training from scratch.

nodes.name: Difficulty signal from mode contrast
nodes.description: A model-specific difficulty proxy is obtained by contrasting mode-conditioned accuracy (e.g. Pass@k) of SHORT (<think>\n\n</think>) versus LONG reasoning mode on the same query.

nodes.name: Root token selects mode
LONG has heavy-tailed length
nodes.description: LONG-mode generation length is heavy-tailed, with a small fraction of queries triggering disproportionately long traces, so routing directly translates into cost control.

nodes.name: Threshold trades accuracy and routing
nodes.description: Larger tau routes more queries to LONG, and intermediate thresholds preserve overall accuracy while reducing LONG usage (Table 1, Fig 3).

nodes.name: SFT for mode selection
nodes.description: Offline synthesis produces paired reasoning and non-reasoning responses via forced chat templates, and SFT on self-generated correct samples teaches mode-following at the template level.

nodes.name: RPO updates only root token
nodes.description: RPO restricts gradient updates to the single initial branching token (T=1) with group-normalized per-mode advantages and KL regularization to the post-SFT reference, treating the rest of the rollout as environment output.

nodes.name: Memory efficiency
nodes.description: Since backprop activation memory scales with the number of updated tokens, setting T=1 removes the linear dependence on CoT length, cutting peak VRAM for long-context GRPO (Table 2).

nodes.name: Training compute savings
nodes.description: With matched accounting on an 8B model, RPO reduces total training compute to about 0.02x that of AdaptThink (Table 5).

nodes.name: RPO improves accuracy-routing tradeoff
nodes.description: On larger and mid-scale backbones RPO reduces Think% with modest accuracy change, e.g. Qwen3-8B Avg Think% 57.3% to 44.8% with Pass@1 63.8% to 62.0% (RAR 0.90 to 0.72), and Exaone4-1.2B Think% 43.4% to 23.6% (RAR 0.85 to 0.49).

nodes.name: SFT already enables routing
nodes.description: SFT alone strongly reduces Think% and tokens, and RPO then refines the root decision to match query difficulty, with direction configuration-dependent.

nodes.name: Comparison with AdaptThink
nodes.description: On R1-1.5B RPO routes 20.5% to LONG with average accuracy 51.3 (RAR 0.96); AdaptThink reaches Avg P@1 56.5 (RAR 0.74) at a far larger training budget, so the two are points on a budget-accuracy frontier.

nodes.name: Controllable operating points
nodes.description: Intermediate RPO checkpoints give multiple feasible Think%/Pass@1 operating points, so a checkpoint can be chosen to satisfy a compute budget, but the frontier depends on the RL prompt set.

isolated_nodes.name: Root confidence weakly calibrated
isolated_nodes.description: The root SHORT confidence p_short is informative but sensitive to bucket composition and only weakly calibrated to query difficulty (Fig 6, ECE/MCE).

isolated_nodes.name: Gains configuration-dependent
isolated_nodes.description: On Qwen3-1.7B post-SFT routing already saturates achievable RAR, and on Qwen3-32B (LoRA) RPO traces a comparable but not dominating frontier, so RPO is a controllable routing layer rather than a replacement for SFT.

isolated_nodes.name: Limited to binary routing
isolated_nodes.description: The method optimizes only the binary reasoning decision, not intra-mode behavior such as how long to think, and has not been evaluated on agentic tasks.

isolated_nodes.name: Generalizes to science and code
isolated_nodes.description: RPO also improves the accuracy-routing tradeoff on LiveCodeBench and GPQA-Diamond across models (Table 6).

structural_reasoning: Overthinking and training-cost hurdles motivate a root-token router; its definition, SFT initialization and RPO objective lead to efficiency and accuracy-routing results. Calibration and limitations are isolated.
